data.body:
Phase 1 confirmed RCA (before repair):

Root cause: the session-scoped provenance fixture caches parsing but not graph structure. `_enclosing` at tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py:377 rebuilds a full child→parent map with `ast.walk` for every lookup. `_verdict` at :433 then, for every parameter hop, iterates every `src/rebar/**/*.py` and walks each cached tree again to rediscover calls to the owner (:464-479). `_run_request_sites` repeats enclosing lookup at :494. Thus AST allocation is gone, but equivalent parent and caller relationships are recomputed millions of times.

Runtime proof: the instrumented cold-process reproduction observed ~9.54 million `ast.walk` node iterations and ~130.9 million Python calls while producing the same 24 ordered `(key, expression, verdict)` tuples. Gerrit run 31778457611 measured this fixture setup at 49.96s/53.03s/53.58s across Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13, ruling out parse I/O and individual assertion bodies as the dominant explanation.

Legitimacy: classified DEFECT against the explicit requirement that individual tests be negligible wall-clock time without reducing behavioral/contract coverage, and this ticket’s acceptance criteria requiring each parsed tree to contribute to caller/parent indexing once while preserving all 24 tuples and four guards.

Expected post-fix behavior: immutable parent/enclosing-function and caller indices are built once from each already-cached tree; `_verdict` queries them; exact ordered tuples and guard verdicts remain unchanged. Caller-dependency sweep: `_enclosing` and this `_verdict` are private helpers confined to this test module; their callers depend on semantic verdicts, not repeated whole-tree traversal. No behavioral dependency blocks the optimization. Phase 2 is unlocked.
